subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What trust model should OpenClaw enforce for SKILL.md skills before prompt loading and capability use?
rationale: Current code has advisory provenance, but choosing trust roots, revocation, unsigned compatibility, profile modes, and runtime enforcement is a security/product boundary that automation should not invent.

options.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
options.body: Specify trusted metadata, signature/digest verification, unsigned behavior, revocation, install/update persistence, runtime loader enforcement, and docs/tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep verification advisory for now
options.body: Leave install provenance and verify commands as user-visible risk signals without blocking or downgrading unsigned skills at runtime.

options.title: Enforce unsigned restrictions immediately
options.body: Add a fail-closed or reduced-capability path for unsigned skills now, accepting compatibility risk for existing community skills.

recommendation.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
recommendation.body: Specify trusted metadata, signature/digest verification, unsigned behavior, revocation, install/update persistence, runtime loader enforcement, and docs/tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible review and feature-history signal across the native skill, ClawHub, and security-product boundary for this issue family.
